findings.text: The Purana texts agree on the early line from Sahasrajit through Śatajit to Haihaya. Dharma and Dharmanetra follow in the texts that carry them, and the Index gives the same father at each step where it has an entry. In the Viṣṇu, Garuda, Linga and Matsya texts the line then runs on to Mahiṣmat.
warnings: names the matsya but cites none of its verses

findings.text: The name after Kunti differs by text. The Viṣṇu texts have Sahajit/Sāhaṃjit, the Garuda has Sāhañji, the Linga has Saṃjaya and the Matsya has Saṃhata. The Index lists a Saṃjaya under another father, so it is unclear whether this is one king under variant names or different people.

Texts differ on who follows Kṛtavīrya. The Viṣṇu (critical edition), Linga and Matsya texts make Arjuna his son, while the Brahmāṇḍa gives Saṃkṣeya as the next name. The Linga calls the son Kārtavīrya Arjuna, and the Viṣṇu critical edition adds his seven-continent rule and thousand arms.

The Matsya text reads Rudraśreṇya where the Linga and Viṣṇu texts read Bhadraśreṇya, and likewise Kanaka where they read Dhanaka. The Index has entries for Bhadraśreṇya and Dhanaka under the same fathers, so these look like variant spellings of the same kings in one line, not separate lines.

Raychaudhuri and Law both describe the Haihayas as five branches, but their lists differ. Raychaudhuri, citing the Matsya, names Vītihotras, Bhojas, Avantis, Kuṇḍikeras and Tālajaṅghas. Law names Vitihotra, Śāryāta, Bhoja, Āvantaya and Kuṇḍika, so Śāryāta appears in one list and Tālajaṅgha in the other.
